identification: Repackaged github.com/pixel365/domain-normalizer Go library with Windows LuaJIT payload archives; uppercase/lowercase registry archive variants have byte-identical member contents.
basis: README diverts users from the functional Go library to an unrelated obfuscated Lua Windows loader. The loader conditionally broadens Defender exclusions, persists, retrieves remote tasks, and executes downloaded files/scripts. These are not domain-normalization operations.
missing_context: Whether anyone launched either batch file
Remote configuration values and task responses at deployment time
Any later-stage payload or current ownership/activity of the configured network infrastructure
static_review: Reviewed every top-level archive member, including Go implementation, tests, Makefile, manifest, and README. Go implementation performs IDNA normalization and public-suffix parsing; no import-time execution hook was found.
README replaces import and function examples with a raw.githubusercontent.com ZIP URL, and labels that ZIP as Releases, Wiki, and application download.

normalizer_domain_v3.9.zip contains LaunchApp.bat: start init.exe icon.txt; init.exe is a LuaJIT interpreter. domain-normalizer.zip contains Launcher.bat: start lua.exe sync.log, LuaJIT lua.exe, and lua51.dll.

Reconstructed 405 H8/V8 indexed string tables in icon.txt without executing its native code. Independently decoded sync.log decimal escapes, table reversals, and custom Base64 alphabet (1058 entries). Used cleave recovered/folded Lua as a further analysis surface, parsed without syntax errors, and traced alias assignments and calls rather than judging string presence.

Both original Lua programs were also evaluated in a restricted Lua 5.1 environment: no host OS/filesystem/network primitives, no Python builtins, mocked require/FFI/Win32 APIs, and an instruction budget. Both requested ffi and bit, loaded lua51.dll, called GetConsoleWindow and ShowWindow, and requested VirtualAlloc(nil,10,12288,64). Execution stopped at the first FFI native function-pointer cast.

The 10-byte native buffer is 65 48 8b 04 25 60 00 00 00 c3: mov rax, gs:[0x60]; ret. Subsequent source casts the result to PEB*, traverses Ldr.InMemoryOrderModuleList, and parses PE export directories to resolve API pointers.

Recovered Lua dispatch resolves and uses WinExec, CopyFileW, CreateThread, WinInet, registry, token-query, and CryptoAPI random functions. Native thread creation is local; no cross-process injection is inferred.

Configuration gates loader.bypass_defender and loader.autorun. The Defender branch concatenates PowerShell Start-Process with -Verb RunAs, hidden-window arguments, and Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $env:SystemDrive -ExclusionExtension .exe, .dll -Force. This requests elevation rather than proving a UAC bypass or successful elevation.

Persistence source formats schtasks /create /sc daily /st %02d:%02d /f using randomized hours 10..14 and minutes 0..59, appends task names and executable/rundll32 actions, and calls the resolved WinExec wrapper. Other branches write the current-user Run key and StartupApproved state. Actual success depends on configuration and permissions.

Network source initializes http://213.176.73.161, an eth_call request to contract 0x1823A9a0Ec8e0C25dD957D0841e3D41a4474bAdc with selector 0x3bc5de30, multiple Polygon RPC fallback hosts, and ip-api.com /json/. Contract response, active C2 status, and downloaded payloads were not fetched.

Remote task processing enumerates a tasks array and handles file_path/file_name/ext. Source includes executable, DLL/rundll32, native-buffer/thread, batch/cmd, PowerShell, and Lua dofile dispatch paths. HTTP helpers construct task/report requests and multipart bodies; GDI code captures a bitmap using GetDC, CreateDIBSection and BitBlt.
trait_changes: Fixed and renamed executable-copy-subcommand-text: require a complete copy/sync subcommand, eliminating lua.exe sync.log. Narrowed the old unbound cross-argument and move-verb alternatives rather than claiming they establish copying.

Consolidated batch Lua launch detection in process/create/shell/command-mode, including .log and other argument suffixes. Moved dofile execution to process/interpreter/eval/source and required an actual call.

Moved two archive co-occurrence traits from supply-chain hidden-payload to anti-static string reconstruction; names and descriptions no longer claim a linked launch or supply-chain trust violation. Runtime presence now requires content evidence, not a chosen lua.exe filename.

Moved all three thread/API co-occurrence composites from legacy threading/async to process/create/thread, renamed them to describe the required API references, and made the former baseline thread/message and thread/memory/context observations notable. No matcher proves a background-thread, worker-pool, or synchronized-message relationship. The message-queue consumer retains the original three alternatives via a named group; its now-redundant broad process/create leg was removed.
Removed golang-x-net::module-import from library identity. Existing engine-emitted metadata/import/go/... retains dependency import observations.

Added notable Lua literal references for CryptGenRandom and CreateThread, and extended the existing neutral WinExec API-name reference to Lua. These names do not by themselves establish invocation or malicious intent.
reference_audit: Updated copy and Go-identity consumers. All three original threading/async match sets now reside under process/create/thread; the message-queue consumer retains exactly those alternatives through a named group, and its redundant broad process/create leg was removed. Reviewed process/create and process/create/thread selectors: all-legs or needs:1 alternatives retain membership from the pre-existing create-thread atom; new Lua API references intentionally extend source coverage. The string-obfuscation ancestor anti-debug consumer is ELF-only, disjoint from the moved archive/PE/source rule scopes.
